ORCHESTRATOR OVERRIDE (Step 5b, 2026-09-09), resp axis only -- the item-code-to-item-text mapping is unchanged and remains VERIFIED. The S1 Dataset 'Note' sheet states per-item anchors and gives the five negatively-worded items (RSES2,5,6,8,9) a FLIPPED scale (1=Strongly agree..4=Strongly disagree) while the other five run 1=Strongly disagree..4=Strongly agree; the extraction agent transcribed that faithfully. The stored data contradicts the Note sheet, so the shipped option_text was corrected to a UNIFORM 1=Strongly disagree..4=Strongly agree for all ten items. Evidence, computed from the live table (n=260): (1) all 10 within-positive-block correlations are positive (0.51 to 0.86) and all 10 within-negative-block correlations are positive (0.43 to 0.85), but 23 of the 25 cross-block correlations are NEGATIVE (-0.22 to 0.061) -- under the Note sheet's flipped coding all ten items would already point the same way and every correlation would be positive. (2) Cronbach's alpha as stored is 0.74, matching the paper's reported overall ordinal alpha of 0.75; recoding the five negative items to 5-x raises it to 0.82, so the paper itself analysed un-recoded data. (3) The paper's Methods states a uniform scale, 'evaluated on a 4-point Likert scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 4 (strongly agree)', and describes reverse scoring as a step performed to COMPUTE the score, not as the stored coding. (4) Table 2's highest item mean is item 8 at 2.57 (live: 2.6), a negatively-worded item, against 1.9-2.0 for every positively-worded item -- coherent under uniform anchoring in a schizophrenia sample, implausible under the flipped coding, which would make item 8 the highest self-esteem item. (5) The paper fits a hierarchical model with both factors on one general factor, which requires the two factors to correlate positively after recoding; as stored they correlate negatively. The S1 'Note' sheet is therefore wrong about its own data -- a defect in the SOURCE, not in the IRW response data, and worth reporting upstream.
